plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: overbidding risks negative profit if the second-highest exceeds your value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With no useful history (single round), and rational opponents likely truth-telling as well, I should bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit. Discrete $0.1 increments allow an exact bid of 30. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid, second-price auction with independent private values. The dominant strategy is to bid your true value: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks winning and paying more than your value if the top rival value lies between your value and your inflated bid. No history to exploit (round 1/1). With $0.1 increments, bid exactly 35.0. Ties are random, but truth-telling remains optimal in expectation. ]

No history effects in this single round. ]
